Description

Osteopontin, a phosphorylated matrix protein of bone, rises in the synovial fluid and plasma of patients with knee osteoarthritis, and its levels follow radiographic severity. Synoviocytes in the osteoarthritic joint make it and respond to it through CD44 and integrin αvβ3. Mast cells, activated in osteoarthritic joints through IgE and its receptor FcεRI, make osteopontin too. Osteopontin binds CD44 and integrin αv on mast cells and strengthens their IgE-triggered degranulation and migration. Degranulation releases histamine, which sensitises nociceptors through the H1 receptor. A direct action of osteopontin on nociceptors has not been shown.
